# buf_clone

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Clone a buffer with a restricted range and an optional callback.

## Declaration

```objectivec
buf_t buf_clone(buf_t bp, int io_offset, int io_size, void (*iodone)(buf_t, void *), void *arg);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer to clone.
- `io_offset`: Offset, relative to start of data in original buffer, at which new buffer's data will begin.
- `io_size`: Size of buffer region in new buffer, in the sense of buf_count().
- `iodone`: Callback to be called from buf_biodone() when I/O completes, in the sense of buf_setcallback().
- `arg`: Argument to pass to iodone() callback.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

NULL if io_offset/io_size combination is invalid for the buffer to be cloned; otherwise, the new buffer.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Generates a buffer which is identical to its "bp" argument except that it spans a subset of the data of the original. The buffer to be cloned should have been allocated with buf_alloc(). Checks its arguments to make sure that the data subset is coherent. Optionally, adds a callback function and argument to it to be called when I/O completes (as with buf_setcallback(), but B_ASYNC is not set). If the original buffer had a upl set through buf_setupl(), this upl is copied to the new buffer; otherwise, the original's data pointer is used raw. The buffer must be released with buf_free().

# Document: buf_meta_bread

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561871-buf_meta_bread
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1561871-buf_meta_bread

# buf_meta_bread

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Synchronously read a metadata block of a file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
errno_t buf_meta_bread(vnode_t vp, daddr64_t blkno, int size, kauth_cred_t cred, buf_t *bpp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The file from which to read.
- `blkno`: The logical (filesystem) block number to read.
- `size`: Size of block; do not use for sizes \> 4K.
- `cred`: Credential to store and use for reading from disk if data are not already in core.
- `bpp`: Destination pointer for buffer.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success, or an error from buf_biowait().

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

buf_meta_bread() is the traditional way to read a single logical block of a file through the buffer cache. It tries to find the buffer and corresponding page(s) in core, calls VNOP_STRATEGY if necessary to bring the data into memory, and waits for I/O to complete. It should not be used to read blocks of greater than 4K (one VM page) in size; use cluster routines for large reads. Reading meta-data through the traditional buffer cache, unlike reading data, is efficient and encouraged, especially if the blocks being read are significantly smaller than page size.

# buf_breadn

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Read a block from a file with read-ahead.

## Declaration

```objectivec
errno_t buf_breadn(vnode_t vp, daddr64_t blkno, int size, daddr64_t *rablks, int *rasizes, int nrablks, kauth_cred_t cred, buf_t *bpp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The file from which to read.
- `blkno`: The logical (filesystem) block number to read synchronously.
- `size`: Size of block; do not use for sizes \> 4K.
- `rablks`: Array of logical block numbers for asynchronous read-aheads.
- `rasizes`: Array of block sizes for asynchronous read-aheads, each index corresponding to same index in "rablks."
- `nrablks`: Number of entries in read-ahead arrays.
- `cred`: Credential to store and use for reading from disk if data are not already in core.
- `bpp`: Destination pointer for buffer.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success, or an error from buf_biowait().

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

buf_breadn() reads one block synchronously in the style of buf_bread() and fires off a specified set of asynchronous reads to improve the likelihood of future cache hits. It should not be used to read blocks of greater than 4K (one VM page) in size; use cluster routines for large reads. Indeed, the cluster layer is a more efficient choice for reading DATA unless you need some finely-tuned semantics that it cannot provide.

# Document: buf_unmap

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561876-buf_unmap

# buf_unmap

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Release mappings for buffer data.

## Declaration

```objectivec
errno_t buf_unmap(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer whose mapping to find or create.
- `io_addr`: Destination for mapping address.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success, EINVAL if unable to unmap buffer.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

For buffers created through buf_getblk() (i.e. traditional buffer cache usage), buf_unmap() does nothing; buf_brelse() will take care of unmapping. For a B_CLUSTER buffer, i.e. an iobuf whose upl state is managed manually, there are two possibilities. If the buffer was created with an underlying "real" buffer through cluster_bp(), buf_unmap() does nothing; buf_brelse() on the underlying buffer will tear down the mapping. Otherwise, the buffer was created with buf_alloc() and buf_setupl() was subsequently called; buf_map() created the mapping. In this case, buf_unmap() will unmap the buffer.

# Document: buf_setcallback

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561885-buf_setcallback
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1561885-buf_setcallback

# buf_setcallback

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Set a function to be called once when I/O on a buffer completes.

## Declaration

```objectivec
errno_t buf_setcallback(buf_t bp, void (*callback)(buf_t, void *), void *transaction);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer whose callback to set.
- `callback`: function to use as callback.
- `transaction`: Additional argument to callback function.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0; always succeeds.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

A one-shot callout set with buf_setcallback() will be called from buf_biodone() when I/O completes. It will be passed the "transaction" argument as well as the buffer. buf_setcallback() also marks the buffer as B_ASYNC.

# buf_bwrite

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Write a buffer's data to backing store.

## Declaration

```objectivec
errno_t buf_bwrite(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: The buffer to write to disk.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success; errors from buf_biowait().

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Once the data in a buffer has been modified, buf_bwrite() starts sending it to disk by calling VNOP_STRATEGY. Unless B_ASYNC has been set on the buffer (by buf_setflags() or otherwise), data will have been written to disk when buf_bwrite() returns. See Bach (p 56).

# Document: buf_map

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561890-buf_map
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1561890-buf_map

# buf_map

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Get virtual mappings for buffer data.

## Declaration

```objectivec
errno_t buf_map(buf_t bp, caddr_t *io_addr);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer whose mapping to find or create.
- `io_addr`: Destination for mapping address.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success, ENOMEM if unable to map the buffer.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

For buffers created through buf_getblk() (i.e. traditional buffer cache usage), buf_map() just returns the address at which data was mapped by but_getblk(). For a B_CLUSTER buffer, i.e. an iobuf whose upl state is managed manually, there are two possibilities. If the buffer was created with an underlying "real" buffer through cluster_bp(), the mapping of the "real" buffer is returned. Otherwise, the buffer was created with buf_alloc() and buf_setupl() was subsequently called; buf_map() will call ubc_upl_map() to get a mapping for the buffer's upl and return the start of that mapping plus the buffer's upl offset (set in buf_setupl()). In the last case, buf_unmap() must later be called to tear down the mapping. NOTE: buf_map() does not set the buffer data pointer; this must be done with buf_setdataptr().

## See Also

### Buffers

- [buf_alloc](1561906-buf_alloc.md): Allocate an uninitialized buffer.
- [buf_attr](1561894-buf_attr.md): Gets the attributes for this buf.
- [buf_bawrite](1561823-buf_bawrite.md): Start an asychronous write on a buffer.
- [buf_bdwrite](1561858-buf_bdwrite.md): Mark a buffer for delayed write.
- [buf_biodone](1561914-buf_biodone.md): Mark an I/O as completed.

# buf_markeintr

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Mark a buffer as having been interrupted during I/O.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void buf_markeintr(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer to mark.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Waiters for I/O to complete (buf_biowait()) will return with EINTR when woken up. buf_markeintr does not itself do a wakeup.

# Document: buf_strategy

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561893-buf_strategy
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1561893-buf_strategy

# buf_strategy

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Pass an I/O request for a buffer down to the device layer.

## Declaration

```objectivec
errno_t buf_strategy(vnode_t devvp, void *ap);
```

## Parameters

- `devvp`: Device on which to perform I/O
- `ap`: vnop_strategy_args structure (most importantly, a buffer).

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success, or errors from filesystem or device layers.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

This is one of the most important routines in the buffer cache layer. For buffers obtained through buf_getblk, it handles finding physical block numbers for the I/O (with VNOP_BLKTOOFF and VNOP_BLOCKMAP), packaging the I/O into page-sized chunks, and initiating I/O on the disk by calling the device's strategy routine. If a buffer's UPL has been set manually with buf_setupl(), it assumes that the request is already correctly configured with a block number and a size divisible by page size and will just call directly to the device.

# buf_attr

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.7+

- `bp`: Buffer whose attributes to get.

## Return Value

bufattr_t.

# Document: physio

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561895-physio
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1561895-physio

# physio

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Perform I/O on a device to/from target memory described by a uio.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int physio(void (*f_strategy)(buf_t), buf_t bp, dev_t dev, int flags, u_int (*f_minphys)(buf_t), struct uio *uio, int blocksize);
```

## Parameters

- `f_strategy`: Strategy routine to call to initiate I/O.
- `bp`: Buffer to configure and pass to strategy routine; can be NULL.
- `dev`: Device on which to perform I/O.
- `flags`: B_READ or B_WRITE.
- `f_minphys`: Function which calls buf_setcount() to set a byte count which is suitably small for the device in question. Returns byte count that has been set (or unchanged) on the buffer.
- `uio`: UIO describing the I/O operation.
- `blocksize`: Logical block size for this vnode.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success; EFAULT for an invalid uio; errors from buf_biowait().

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

physio() allows I/O directly from a device to user-space memory. It waits for all I/O to complete before returning.
# Document: buf_wcred

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561896-buf_wcred
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1561896-buf_wcred

# buf_wcred

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Get the credential associated with a buffer for writing.

## Declaration

```objectivec
kauth_cred_t buf_wcred(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer whose credential to grab.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Credential if it exists, else NULL.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

No reference is taken; if the credential is to be held on to persistently, an additional reference must be taken with kauth_cred_ref.

# Document: buf_brelse

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561897-buf_brelse
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1561897-buf_brelse

# buf_brelse

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Release any claim to a buffer, sending it back to free lists.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void buf_brelse(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: The buffer to release. @retrn void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

buf_brelse() cleans up buffer state and releases a buffer to the free lists. If the buffer is not marked invalid and its pages are dirty (e.g. a delayed write was made), its data will be commited to backing store. If it is marked invalid, its data will be discarded completely. A valid, cacheable buffer will be put on a list and kept in the buffer hash so it can be found again; otherwise, it will be dissociated from its vnode and treated as empty. Which list a valid buffer is placed on depends on the use of buf_markaged(), whether it is metadata, and the B_LOCKED flag. A B_LOCKED buffer will not be available for reuse by other files, though its data may be paged out. Note that buf_brelse() is intended for use with traditionally allocated buffers.

# buf_setlblkno

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Set logical block number associated with a buffer.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void buf_setlblkno(buf_t bp, daddr64_t lblkno);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer whose logical block number to set.
- `lblkno`: Block number to set.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Logical block number is set on traditionally-used buffers by an argument passed to buf_getblk(), for example by buf_bread().

# Document: buf_clear

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561901-buf_clear
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1561901-buf_clear

# buf_clear

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Zero out the storage associated with a buffer.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void buf_clear(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: The buffer to zero out.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Calls buf_map() to get the buffer's data address; for a B_CLUSTER buffer (one which has had buf_setupl() called on it), it tries to map the buffer's UPL into memory; should only be called once during the life cycle of an iobuf (one allocated with buf_alloc()).

# buf_callback

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Get the function set to be called when I/O on a buffer completes.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void * buf_callback(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer whose callback to get.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success, or errors from filesystem or device layers.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

A function returned by buf_callback was originally set with buf_setcallback().

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561906-buf_alloc
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1561906-buf_alloc

# buf_alloc

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Allocate an uninitialized buffer.

## Declaration

```objectivec
buf_t buf_alloc(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: vnode to associate with the buffer: optionally NULL. If vp is a device file, then the buffer's associated device will be set. If vp is NULL, it can be set later with buf_setvnode().

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

New buffer.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

A buffer returned by buf_alloc() is marked as busy and as an iobuf; it has no storage set up and must be set up using buf_setdataptr() or buf_setupl()/buf_map().

# buf_free

# buf_biowait

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Wait for I/O on a buffer to complete.

## Declaration

```objectivec
errno_t buf_biowait(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: The buffer to wait on.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for a successful wait; nonzero the buffer has been marked as EINTR or had an error set on it.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Waits for I/O on a buffer to finish, as marked by a buf_biodone() call.

# Document: buf_invalidateblks

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561910-buf_invalidateblks
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1561910-buf_invalidateblks

# buf_invalidateblks

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Invalidate all the blocks associated with a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int buf_invalidateblks(vnode_t vp, int flags, int slpflag, int slptimeo);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: The buffer whose data to invalidate.
- `flags`: BUF_WRITE_DATA: write dirty data to disk with VNOP_BWRITE() before kicking buffer cache entries out. BUF_SKIP_META: do not invalidate metadata blocks.
- `slpflag`: Flags to pass to "msleep" while waiting to acquire busy buffers.
- `slptimeo`: Timeout in "hz" (1/100 second) to wait for a buffer to become unbusy before waking from sleep and re-starting the scan.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success, error values from msleep().

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

This function does for all blocks associated with a vnode what buf_invalblkno does for one block. Again, it will only be able to invalidate data which were populated with traditional buffer cache routines, i.e. by buf_getblk() and callers thereof. Unlike buf_invalblkno(), it can be made to write dirty data to disk rather than casting it aside.

# buf_markdelayed

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Mark a buffer as a delayed write: mark it dirty without actually scheduling I/O.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void buf_markdelayed(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer to mark.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Data will be flushed to disk at some later time, not with brelse(). A sync()/fsync() or pressure necessitating reuse of the buffer will cause it to be written back to disk.

# Document: buf_biodone

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561914-buf_biodone
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1561914-buf_biodone

# buf_biodone

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Mark an I/O as completed.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void buf_biodone(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: The buffer to mark as done with I/O.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

buf_biodone() should be called by whosoever decides that an I/O on a buffer is complete; for example, IOStorageFamily. It clears the dirty flag on a buffer and signals on the vnode that a write has completed with vnode_writedone(). If a callout or filter has been set on the buffer, that function is called. In the case of a callout, that function is expected to take care of cleaning up and freeing the buffer. Otherwise, if the buffer is marked B_ASYNC (e.g. it was passed to buf_bawrite()), then buf_biodone() considers itself justified in calling buf_brelse() to return it to free lists--no one is waiting for it. Finally, waiters on the bp (e.g. in buf_biowait()) are woken up.

# buf_size

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Get size of data region allocated to a buffer.

## Declaration

```objectivec
uint32_t buf_size(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer whose size to get.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Size.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

May be larger than amount of valid data in buffer.

# buf_upl

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Get the upl (Universal Page List) associated with a buffer.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void * buf_upl(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer whose upl to grab.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Buffer's upl if it has one, else NULL.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Buffers allocated with buf_alloc() are not returned with a upl, and traditional buffers only have a upl while an I/O is in progress.

# Document: buf_vnode

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561919-buf_vnode

# buf_vnode

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Get the vnode associated with a buffer.

## Declaration

```objectivec
vnode_t buf_vnode(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer whose vnode to retrieve.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Buffer's vnode.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Every buffer is associated with a file. Because there is an I/O in flight, there is an iocount on this vnode; it is returned WITHOUT an extra iocount, and vnode_put() need NOT be called.

## See Also

### Buffers

# Document: buf_setsize

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561921-buf_setsize
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1561921-buf_setsize

# buf_setsize

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Set size of data region allocated to a buffer.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void buf_setsize(buf_t bp, uint32_t);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer whose size to set.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

May be larger than amount of valid data in buffer. Should be used by code which is manually providing storage for an iobuf, one allocated with buf_alloc().

# Document: buf_device

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561922-buf_device
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1561922-buf_device

# buf_device

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Get the device ID associated with a buffer.

## Declaration

```objectivec
dev_t buf_device(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer whose device ID to retrieve.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Device id.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

In traditional buffer use, this value is NODEV until buf_strategy() is called unless buf_getblk() was passed a device vnode. It is set on an iobuf if buf_alloc() is passed a device vnode or if buf_setdevice() is called.

**Interface language:** Objective-C

## Declaration

```objectivec
uint32_t buf_dirtyoff(buf_t bp);
```

# Document: buf_blkno

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561926-buf_blkno
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1561926-buf_blkno

# buf_blkno

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Get physical block number associated with a buffer, in the sense of VNOP_BLOCKMAP.

## Declaration

```objectivec
daddr64_t buf_blkno(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer whose physical block number to get.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Block number.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

When a buffer's physical block number is the same is its logical block number, then the physical block number is considered uninitialized. A physical block number of -1 indicates that there is no valid physical mapping (e.g. the logical block is invalid or corresponds to a sparse region in a file). Physical block number is normally set by the cluster layer or by buf_getblk().

# buf_reset

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Reset I/O flag state on a buffer.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void buf_reset(buf_t bp, int32_t flags);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer whose flags to grab.
- `flags`: Flags to set on buffer: B_READ, B_WRITE, B_ASYNC, B_NOCACHE.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Clears current flags on a buffer (internal and external) and allows some new flags to be set. Used perhaps to prepare an iobuf for reuse.

# Document: buf_getblk

Source path: documentation/kernel/1561932-buf_getblk
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1561932-buf_getblk

# buf_getblk

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Traditional buffer cache routine to get a buffer corresponding to a logical block in a file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
buf_t buf_getblk(vnode_t vp, daddr64_t blkno, int size, int slpflag, int slptimeo, int operation);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: File for which to get block.
- `blkno`: Logical block number.
- `size`: Size of block.
- `slpflag`: Flag to pass to msleep() while waiting for buffer to become unbusy.
- `slptimeo`: Time, in milliseconds, to wait for buffer to become unbusy. 0 means to wait indefinitely.
- `operation`: BLK_READ: want a read buffer. BLK_WRITE: want a write buffer. BLK_META: want a metadata buffer. BLK_ONLYVALID: only return buffers which are found in core (do not allocate anew), and do not change buffer size. The last remark means that if a given logical block is found in core with a different size than what is requested, the buffer size will not be modified.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Buffer found in core or newly allocated, either containing valid data or ready for I/O.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

buf_getblk() gets a buffer, not necessarily containing valid data, representing a block in a file. A metadata buffer will be returned with its own zone-allocated storage, managed by the traditional buffer-cache layer, whereas data buffers will be returned hooked into backing by the UBC (which in fact controls the caching of data). buf_getblk() first looks for the buffer header in cache; if the buffer is in-core but busy, buf_getblk() will wait for it to become unbusy, depending on the slpflag and slptimeo parameters. If the buffer is found unbusy and is a metadata buffer, it must already contain valid data and will be returned directly; data buffers will have a UPL configured to prepare for interaction with the underlying UBC. If the buffer is found in core, it will be marked as such and buf_fromcache() will return truth. A buffer is allocated and initialized (but not filled with data) if none is found in core. buf_bread(), buf_breadn(), buf_meta_bread(), and buf_meta_breadn() all return buffers obtained with buf_getblk().

# buf_fromcache

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Check if a buffer's data was found in core.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int buf_fromcache(buf_t bp);
```

## Parameters

- `bp`: Buffer to test.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Nonzero if we got this buffer's data without doing I/O, 0 if not.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Will return truth after a buf_getblk that finds a valid buffer in the cache or the relevant data in core (but not in a buffer).

# Document: vnode_get

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562083-vnode_get
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562083-vnode_get

# vnode_get

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Increase the iocount on a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_get(vnode_t);
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success, ENOENT if the vnode is dead and without existing io-reference.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If vnode_get() succeeds, the resulting io-reference must be dropped with vnode_put(). This function succeeds unless the vnode in question is dead or in the process of dying AND the current iocount is zero. This means that it can block an ongoing reclaim which is blocked behind some other iocount.

On success, vnode_get() returns with an iocount held on the vnode; this type of reference is intended to be held only for short periods of time (e.g. across a function call) and provides a strong guarantee about the life of the vnode; vnodes with positive iocounts cannot be recycled, and an iocount is required for any operation on a vnode. However, vnode_get() does not provide any guarantees about the identity of the vnode it is called on; unless there is a known existing iocount on the vnode at time the call is made, it could be recycled and put back in use before the vnode_get() succeeds, so the caller may be referencing a completely different vnode than was intended. vnode_getwithref() and vnode_getwithvid() provide guarantees about vnode identity.

# Document: vnode_authorize

# vnode_authorize

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Authorize a kauth-style action on a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_authorize(vnode_t vp, vnode_t dvp, kauth_action_t action, vfs_context_t ctx);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: Vnode on which to authorize action.
- `dvp`: Parent of "vp," can be NULL.
- `action`: Action to authorize, e.g. KAUTH_VNODE_READ_DATA. See bsd/sys/kauth.h.
- `ctx`: Context for which to authorize actions.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

EACCESS if permission is denied. 0 if operation allowed. Various errors from lower layers.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Operations on dead vnodes are always allowed (though never do anything).

# Document: vnode_close

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562091-vnode_close
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562091-vnode_close

# vnode_close

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Close a file as opened with vnode_open().

## Declaration

```objectivec
errno_t vnode_close(vnode_t vp, int flags, vfs_context_t ctx);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to close.
- `flags`: Flags to close: FWASWRITTEN indicates that the file was written to.
- `ctx`: Context against which to validate operation.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success or an error from the filesystem.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

vnode_close() drops the refcount (persistent reference) picked up in vnode_open() and calls down to the filesystem with VNOP_CLOSE. It should be called with both an iocount and a refcount on the vnode and will drop both.

# Document: vn_rdwr

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562098-vn_rdwr
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562098-vn_rdwr

# vn_rdwr

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Read from or write to a file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vn_rdwr(enum uio_rw rw, struct vnode *vp, caddr_t base, int len, off_t offset, enum uio_seg segflg, int ioflg, kauth_cred_t cred, int *aresid, proc_t p);
```

## Parameters

- `rw`: UIO_READ for a read, UIO_WRITE for a write.
- `vp`: The vnode on which to perform I/O.
- `base`: Start of buffer into which to read or from which to write data.
- `len`: Length of buffer.
- `offset`: Offset within the file at which to start I/O.
- `segflg`: What kind of address "base" is. See uio_seg definition in sys/uio.h. UIO_SYSSPACE for kernelspace, UIO_USERSPACE for userspace. UIO_USERSPACE32 and UIO_USERSPACE64 are in general preferred, but vn_rdwr will make sure that has the correct address sizes.
- `ioflg`: Defined in vnode.h, e.g. IO_NOAUTH, IO_NOCACHE.
- `cred`: Credential to pass down to filesystem for authentication.
- `aresid`: Destination for amount of requested I/O which was not completed, as with uio_resid().
- `p`: Process requesting I/O.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success; errors from filesystem, and EIO if did not perform all requested I/O and the "aresid" parameter is NULL.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

vn_rdwr() abstracts the details of constructing a uio and picking a vnode operation to allow simple in-kernel file I/O.
# Document: vn_getpath

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562103-vn_getpath
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562103-vn_getpath

# vn_getpath

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Construct the path to a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vn_getpath(struct vnode *vp, char *pathbuf, int *len);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose path to obtain.
- `pathbuf`: Destination for pathname; should be of size MAXPATHLEN
- `len`: Destination for length of resulting path string. Result will include NULL-terminator in count--that is, "len" will be strlen(pathbuf) + 1.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success or an error code.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Paths to vnodes are not always straightforward: a file with multiple hard-links will have multiple pathnames, and it is sometimes impossible to determine a vnode's full path. vn_getpath() will not enter the filesystem.
# Document: vnode_authattr

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562106-vnode_authattr
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562106-vnode_authattr

# vnode_authattr

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Given a vnode_attr structure, determine what kauth-style actions must be authorized in order to set those attributes.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_authattr(vnode_t vp, struct vnode_attr *vap, kauth_action_t *actionp, vfs_context_t ctx);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode on which to authorize action.
- `vap`: Pointer to vnode_attr struct containing desired attributes to set and their values.
- `actionp`: Destination for set of actions to authorize
- `ctx`: Context for which to authorize actions.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 (and a result in "actionp" for success. Otherwise, an error code.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

vnode_authorize requires kauth-style actions; if we want to set a vnode_attr structure on a vnode, we need to translate the set of attributes to a set of kauth-style actions. This routine will return errors for certain obviously disallowed, or incoherent, actions.

# Document: vn_bwrite

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562107-vn_bwrite
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562107-vn_bwrite

# vn_bwrite

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

System-provided implementation of "bwrite" vnop.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vn_bwrite(struct vnop_bwrite_args *ap);
```

## Parameters

- `ap`: Standard parameters to a bwrite vnop.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Results of buf_bwrite directly.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

This routine is available for filesystems which do not want to implement their own "bwrite" vnop. It just calls buf_bwrite() without modifying its arguments.
# Document: vnode_uncache_credentials

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562109-vnode_uncache_credentials
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562109-vnode_uncache_credentials

# vnode_uncache_credentials

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.5+

Clear out cached credentials on a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void vnode_uncache_credentials(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose cache to clear.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

When we authorize an action on a vnode, we cache the credential that was authorized and the actions it was authorized for in case a similar request follows. This function destroys that caching.

# vnode_create

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Create and initialize a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
errno_t vnode_create(uint32_t flavor, uint32_t size, void *data, vnode_t *vpp);
```

## Parameters

- `flavor`: Should be VNCREATE_FLAVOR.
- `size`: Size of the struct vnode_fsparam in "data".
- `data`: Pointer to a struct vnode_fsparam containing initialization information.
- `vpp`: Pointer to a vnode pointer, to be filled in with newly created vnode.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success, error code otherwise.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Returns wth an iocount held on the vnode which must eventually be dropped with vnode_put().

# Document: vnode_vid

# vnode_vid

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Return a vnode's vid (generation number), which is constant from creation until reclaim.

## Declaration

```objectivec
uint32_t vnode_vid(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose vid to grab.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The vnode's vid.

# Document: vflush

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562120-vflush
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562120-vflush

# vflush

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Reclaim the vnodes for a mount.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vflush(struct mount *mp, struct vnode *skipvp, int flags);
```

## Parameters

- `mp`: The mount with the vnodes to terminate.
- `skipvp`: A specific vnode to not reclaim or to let interrupt an unforced flush.
- `flags`: Controls that indicate how to handle vnodes.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success, EBUSY if vnodes were busy and FORCECLOSE was not set.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

This function is used to clear out the vnodes associated with a mount as part of the unmount process. Its parameters can determine which vnodes to skip in the process and whether in-use vnodes should be forcibly reclaimed. File systems should call this function from their unmount code, because VFS code will always call it with SKIPROOT | SKIPSWAP | SKIPSYSTEM; file systems must take care of such vnodes themselves.
# Document: vnode_rele

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562121-vnode_rele
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562121-vnode_rele

# vnode_rele

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Decrement the usecount on a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void vnode_rele(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose usecount to drop.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

vnode_rele() is called to relese a persistent reference on a vnode. Releasing the last usecount opens the door for a vnode to be reused as a new file; it also triggers a VNOP_INACTIVE call to the filesystem, though that will not happen immediately if there are outstanding iocount references.

# Document: vfs_context_is64bit

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562122-vfs_context_is64bit
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562122-vfs_context_is64bit

# vfs_context_is64bit

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Determine if a vfs_context_t corresponds to a 64-bit user process.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vfs_context_is64bit(vfs_context_t ctx);
```

## Parameters

- `ctx`: Context to examine.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Nonzero if context is of 64-bit process, 0 otherwise.
# Document: vnode_setnoreadahead

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562123-vnode_setnoreadahead
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562123-vnode_setnoreadahead

# vnode_setnoreadahead

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Set a vnode to not have data speculatively read in in hopes of hitting in cache.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void vnode_setnoreadahead(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode on which to prevent readahead.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

# Document: vnode_open

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562149-vnode_open
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562149-vnode_open

# vnode_open

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Open a file identified by a path--roughly speaking an in-kernel open(2).

## Declaration

```objectivec
errno_t vnode_open(const char *path, int fmode, int cmode, int flags, vnode_t *vpp, vfs_context_t ctx);
```

## Parameters

- `path`: Path to look up.
- `fmode`: e.g. O_NONBLOCK, O_APPEND; see bsd/sys/fcntl.h.
- `cmode`: Permissions with which to create file if it does not exist.
- `flags`: Same as vnode_lookup().
- `vpp`: Destination for vnode.
- `ctx`: Context with which to authorize open/creation.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success or an error code.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If vnode_open() succeeds, it returns with both an iocount and a usecount on the returned vnode. These must be released eventually; the iocount should be released with vnode_put() as soon as any initial operations on the vnode are over, whereas the usecount should be released via vnode_close().

# vnode_isfifo

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Determine if a vnode is a named pipe.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_isfifo(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

# Document: vnode_vfsmaxsymlen

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562159-vnode_vfsmaxsymlen
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562159-vnode_vfsmaxsymlen

# vnode_vfsmaxsymlen

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Determine the maximum length of a symbolic link for the filesystem on which a vnode resides.

## Declaration

```objectivec
uint32_t vnode_vfsmaxsymlen(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode for which to get filesystem symlink size cap.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Max symlink length.

# Document: vnode_needssnapshots

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562160-vnode_needssnapshots
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562160-vnode_needssnapshots

# vnode_needssnapshots

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.7+

Check if a vnode needs snapshots events (regardless of its ctime status)

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_needssnapshots(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to test.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Nonzero if vnode needs snapshot events, 0 otherwise

# vnode_isnamedstream

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.5+

Determine if a vnode is a named stream.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_isnamedstream(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to test.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Nonzero if the vnode is a named stream, 0 otherwise.

# vnode_vfs64bitready

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Determine if the filesystem to which a vnode belongs is marked as ready to interact with 64-bit user processes.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_vfs64bitready(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose filesystem to examine.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Nonzero if filesystem is marked ready for 64-bit interactions; 0 otherwise.

# Document: vn_path_package_check

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562172-vn_path_package_check
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562172-vn_path_package_check

# vn_path_package_check

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Figure out if a path corresponds to a macOS package.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vn_path_package_check(vnode_t vp, char *path, int pathlen, int *component);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: Unused.
- `path`: Path to check.
- `pathlen`: Size of path buffer.
- `component`: Set to index of start of last path component if the path is found to be a package. Set to -1 if the path is not a known package type.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 unless some parameter was invalid, in which case EINVAL is returned. Determine package-ness by checking what \*component is set to.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Determines if the extension on a path is a known macOS extension type.
# Document: vnode_vtype

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562175-vnode_vtype
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562175-vnode_vtype

# vnode_vtype

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Return a vnode's type.

## Declaration

```objectivec
enum vtype vnode_vtype(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose type to grab.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The vnode's type.

# Document: vnode_isinuse

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562179-vnode_isinuse
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562179-vnode_isinuse

# vnode_isinuse

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Determine if the number of persistent (usecount) references on a vnode is greater than a given count.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_isinuse(vnode_t vp, int refcnt);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose use-status to check.
- `refcnt`: The threshold for saying that a vnode is in use.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

vnode_isinuse() compares a vnode's usecount (corresponding to vnode_ref() calls) to its refcnt parameter (the number of references the caller expects to be on the vnode). Note that "kusecount" references, corresponding to parties interested only in event notifications, e.g. open(..., O_EVTONLY), are not counted towards the total; the comparison is (usecount - kusecount \> recnt). It is also important to note that the result is only a snapshot; usecounts can change from moment to moment, and the result of vnode_isinuse may no longer be correct the very moment that the caller receives it.

# vnode_authattr_new

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Initialize and validate file creation parameters with respect to the current context.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_authattr_new(vnode_t dvp, struct vnode_attr *vap, int noauth, vfs_context_t ctx);
```

## Parameters

- `dvp`: The directory in which creation will occur.
- `vap`: Pointer to vnode_attr struct containing desired attributes to set and their values.
- `noauth`: If 1, treat the caller as the superuser, i.e. do not check permissions.
- `ctx`: Context for which to authorize actions.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

KAUTH_RESULT_ALLOW for success, an error to indicate invalid or disallowed attributes.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

vnode_authattr_new() will fill in unitialized values in the vnode_attr struct with defaults, and will validate the structure with respect to the current context for file creation.

# Document: vnode_getparent

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562185-vnode_getparent
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562185-vnode_getparent

# vnode_getparent

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Get an iocount on the parent of a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
vnode_t vnode_getparent(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose parent to grab.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Parent if available, else NULL.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

A vnode's parent may change over time or be reclaimed, so vnode_getparent() may return different results at different times (e.g. a multiple-hardlink file). The parent is returned with an iocount which must subsequently be dropped with vnode_put().

# Document: vnode_isnocache

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562192-vnode_isnocache
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562192-vnode_isnocache

# vnode_isnocache

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Check if a vnode is set to not have its data cached in memory (i.e. we write-through to disk and always read from disk).

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_isnocache(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to test.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Nonzero if vnode is set to not have data chached, 0 otherwise.

# Document: cache_lookup

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562195-cache_lookup
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562195-cache_lookup

# cache_lookup

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Check for a filename in a directory using the VFS name cache.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int cache_lookup(vnode_t dvp, vnode_t *vpp, struct componentname *cnp);
```

## Parameters

- `dvp`: Directory in which lookup is occurring.
- `vpp`: Destination for vnode pointer.
- `cnp`: Various data about lookup, e.g. filename and intended operation.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

ENOENT: the filesystem has previously added a negative entry with cache_enter() to indicate that there is no file of the given name in "dp." -1: successfully found a cached vnode (vpp is set). 0: No data in the cache, or operation is CRETE/RENAME.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

cache_lookup() will flush negative cache entries and return 0 if the operation of the cn_nameiop is CREATE or RENAME. Often used from the filesystem during a lookup vnop. The filesystem will be called to if there is a negative cache entry for a file, so it can make sense to initially check for negative entries (and possibly lush them).

# Document: vnode_setmultipath

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562201-vnode_setmultipath
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562201-vnode_setmultipath

# vnode_setmultipath

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.5+

Mark a vnode as being reachable by multiple paths, i.e. as a hard link.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void vnode_setmultipath(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to mark.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

"Multipath" vnodes can be reached through more than one entry in the filesystem, and so must be handled differently for caching and event notification purposes. A filesystem should mark a vnode with multiple hardlinks this way.

# Document: vnode_islnk

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562202-vnode_islnk
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562202-vnode_islnk

# vnode_islnk

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Determine if a vnode is a symbolic link.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_islnk(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to test.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Nonzero if the vnode is of type VLNK, 0 otherwise.

# Document: vnode_removefsref

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562210-vnode_removefsref
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562210-vnode_removefsref

# vnode_removefsref

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Mark a vnode as no longer being stored in a filesystem hash.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_removefsref(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to unmark.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Always 0.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Should only be called once on a vnode (during a reclaim), and only after the vnode has either been created with VNFS_ADDFSREF or marked by vnode_addfsref().

# Document: vnode_isrecycled

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562214-vnode_isrecycled

# vnode_isrecycled

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.5+

Check if a vnode is dead or in the process of being killed (recycled).

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_isrecycled(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to test.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Nonzero if vnode is dead or being recycled, 0 otherwise.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

This is only a snapshot: a vnode may start to be recycled, or go from dead to in use, at any time.

# Document: vnode_addfsref

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562216-vnode_addfsref
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562216-vnode_addfsref

# vnode_addfsref

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Mark a vnode as being stored in a filesystem hash.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_addfsref(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to mark.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Always 0.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Should only be called once on a vnode, and never if that vnode was created with VNFS_ADDFSREF. There should be a corresponding call to vnode_removefsref() when the vnode is reclaimed; VFS assumes that a n unused vnode will not be marked as referenced by a filesystem.

# Document: vfs_context_current

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562223-vfs_context_current
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562223-vfs_context_current

# vfs_context_current

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.5+

Get the vfs_context for the current thread, or the kernel context if there is no context for current thread.

## Declaration

```objectivec
vfs_context_t vfs_context_current(void);
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Context for current thread, or kernel context if thread context is unavailable.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Kexts should not use this function--it is preferred to use vfs_context_create(NULL) and vfs_context_rele(), which ensure proper reference counting of underlying structures.
# Document: cache_purge

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562225-cache_purge
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562225-cache_purge

# cache_purge

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Remove all data relating to a vnode from the namecache.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void cache_purge(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to purge.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Will flush all hardlinks to the vnode as well as all children (should any exist). Logical to use when cached data about a vnode becomes invalid, for instance in an unlink.

# Document: vnode_israge

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562229-vnode_israge
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562229-vnode_israge

# vnode_israge

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Check if a vnode is marked for rapid aging

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_israge(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to test.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Nonzero if vnode is marked for rapid aging, 0 otherwise

# vnode_isblk

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Determine if a vnode is a block device special file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_isblk(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to test.

## Return Value

Nonzero if the vnode is of type VBLK, 0 otherwise.

# Document: vnode_recycle

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562237-vnode_recycle
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562237-vnode_recycle

# vnode_recycle

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Cause a vnode to be reclaimed and prepared for reuse.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_recycle(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to recycle.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

1 if the vnode was reclaimed (i.e. there were no existing references), 0 if it was only marked for future reclaim.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Like all vnode KPIs, must be called with an iocount on the target vnode. vnode_recycle() will mark that vnode for reclaim when all existing references are dropped.

# Document: vnode_ref

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562240-vnode_ref
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562240-vnode_ref

# vnode_ref

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Increment the usecount on a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_ref(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode on which to obtain a persistent reference.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success; ENOENT if the vnode is dead or in the process of being recycled AND the calling thread is not the vnode owner.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If vnode_ref() succeeds, the resulting usecount must be released with vnode_rele(). vnode_ref() is called to obtain a persistent reference on a vnode. This type of reference does not provide the same strong guarantee that a vnode will persist as does an iocount--it merely ensures that a vnode will not be reused to represent a different file. However, a usecount may be held for extended periods of time, whereas an iocount is intended to be obtained and released quickly as part of performing a vnode operation. A holder of a usecount must call vnode_getwithref()/vnode_put() in order to perform any operations on that vnode.

# Document: vnode_lookup

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562245-vnode_lookup
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562245-vnode_lookup

# vnode_lookup

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Convert a path into a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
errno_t vnode_lookup(const char *path, int flags, vnode_t *vpp, vfs_context_t ctx);
```

## Parameters

- `path`: Path to look up.
- `flags`: VNODE_LOOKUP_NOFOLLOW: do not follow symbolic links. VNODE_LOOKUP_NOCROSSMOUNT: do not cross mount points.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Results 0 for success or an error code.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

This routine is a thin wrapper around xnu-internal lookup routines; if successful, it returns with an iocount held on the resulting vnode which must be dropped with vnode_put().

# vnode_isswap

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.5+

Determine if a vnode is being used as a swap file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_isswap(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to test.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Nonzero if the vnode is being used as swap, 0 otherwise.

# Document: vfs_context_suser

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562261-vfs_context_suser
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562261-vfs_context_suser

# vfs_context_suser

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Determine if a vfs_context_t corresponds to the superuser.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vfs_context_suser(vfs_context_t ctx);
```

## Parameters

- `ctx`: Context to examine.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Nonzero if context belongs to superuser, 0 otherwise.

# Document: vnode_getattr

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562270-vnode_getattr
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562270-vnode_getattr

# vnode_getattr

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Get vnode attributes.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_getattr(vnode_t vp, struct vnode_attr *vap, vfs_context_t ctx);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose attributes to grab.
- `vap`: Structure containing: 1) A list of requested attributes 2) Space to indicate which attributes are supported and being returned 3) Space to return attributes.
- `ctx`: Context for authentication.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success or an error code.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Desired attributes are set with VATTR_SET_ACTIVE and VNODE_ATTR\* macros. Supported attributes are determined after call with VATTR_IS_SUPPORTED.

# Document: vnode_isdir

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562276-vnode_isdir
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562276-vnode_isdir

# vnode_isdir

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Determine if a vnode is a directory.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_isdir(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to test.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Nonzero if the vnode is of type VDIR, 0 otherwise.

# Document: vnode_put

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562280-vnode_put
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562280-vnode_put

# vnode_put

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Decrement the iocount on a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_put(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose iocount to drop.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Always 0.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

vnode_put() is called to indicate that a vnode is no longer in active use. It removes the guarantee that a vnode will not be recycled. This routine should be used to release io references no matter how they were obtained.

## Declaration

```objectivec
const char * vnode_getname(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose name to grab.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The name, or NULL if unavailable.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Not all vnodes have names, and vnode names can change (notably, hardlinks). Use this routine at your own risk. The string is returned with a refcount incremented in the cache; callers must call vnode_putname() to release that reference.

# Document: cache_enter

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562285-cache_enter
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562285-cache_enter

# cache_enter

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Add a (name,vnode) entry to the VFS namecache.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void cache_enter(vnode_t dvp, vnode_t vp, struct componentname *cnp);
```

## Parameters

- `dvp`: Directory in which file lives.
- `vp`: File to add to cache. A non-NULL vp is stored for rapid access; a NULL vp indicates that there is no such file in the directory and speeds future failed lookups.
- `cnp`: Various data about lookup, e.g. filename and intended operation.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Generally used to add a cache entry after a successful filesystem-level lookup or to add a negative entry after one which did not find its target.

# Document: vnode_settag

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562288-vnode_settag
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562288-vnode_settag

# vnode_settag

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Set a vnode filesystem-specific "tag."

## Declaration

```objectivec
void vnode_settag(vnode_t vp, int tag);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose tag to set.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Sets a tag indicating which filesystem a vnode belongs to, e.g. VT_HFS, VT_UDF, VT_ZFS. The kernel never inspects this data, though the filesystem tags are defined in vnode.h; it is for the benefit of user programs via getattrlist.

# Document: vnode_vfstypenum

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562295-vnode_vfstypenum
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562295-vnode_vfstypenum

# vnode_vfstypenum

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Get the "type number" of the filesystem to which a vnode belongs.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_vfstypenum(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose filesystem to examine.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The type number of the fileystem to which the vnode belongs.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

This is an archaic construct; most filesystems are assigned a type number based on the order in which they are registered with the system.

# Document: vnode_getwithref

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562306-vnode_getwithref
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562306-vnode_getwithref

# vnode_getwithref

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Increase the iocount on a vnode on which a usecount (persistent reference) is held.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_getwithref(vnode_t vp);
```

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 for success, ENOENT if the vnode is dead, in the process of being reclaimed, or has been recycled and reused.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If vnode_getwithref() succeeds, the resulting io-reference must be dropped with vnode_put(). vnode_getwithref() will succeed on dead vnodes; it should fail with ENOENT on vnodes which are in the process of being reclaimed. Because it is only called with a usecount on the vnode, the caller is guaranteed that the vnode has not been reused for a different file, though it may now be dead and have deadfs vnops (which return errors like EIO, ENXIO, ENOTDIR). On success, vnode_getwithref() returns with an iocount held on the vnode; this type of reference is intended to be held only for short periods of time (e.g. across a function call) and provides a strong guarantee about the life of the vnode. vnodes with positive iocounts cannot be recycled. An iocount is required for any operation on a vnode.

# vnode_isnoreadahead

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Check if a vnode is set to not have data speculatively read in in hopes of future cache hits.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_isnoreadahead(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

# Document: vfs_context_ucred

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562308-vfs_context_ucred
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562308-vfs_context_ucred

# vfs_context_ucred

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Get the credential associated with a vfs_context_t.

## Declaration

```objectivec
kauth_cred_t vfs_context_ucred(vfs_context_t ctx);
```

## Parameters

- `ctx`: Context whose associated process to find.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Process if available, NULL otherwise.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Succeeds if and only if the context has a thread, the thread has a task, and the task has a BSD proc.
# Document: vnode_fsnode

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562316-vnode_fsnode
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562316-vnode_fsnode

# vnode_fsnode

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Gets the filesystem-specific data associated with a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void * vnode_fsnode(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose data to grab.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The filesystem-specific data, directly.

# Document: vnode_setnocache

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562318-vnode_setnocache
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562318-vnode_setnocache

# vnode_setnocache

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Set a vnode to not have its data cached in memory (i.e. we write-through to disk and always read from disk).

## Declaration

```objectivec
void vnode_setnocache(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose flags to set.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

# vnode_mountedhere

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Returns a pointer to a mount placed on top of a vnode, should it exist.

## Declaration

```objectivec
mount_t vnode_mountedhere(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode from whom to take the covering mount.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Pointer to mount covering a vnode, or NULL if none exists.

# Document: vnode_tag

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562337-vnode_tag
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562337-vnode_tag

# vnode_tag

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Get the vnode filesystem-specific "tag."

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_tag(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose tag to grab.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The tag.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Gets the tag indicating which filesystem a vnode belongs to, e.g. VT_HFS, VT_UDF, VT_ZFS. The kernel never inspects this data, though the filesystem tags are defined in vnode.h; it is for the benefit of user programs via getattrlist.

# Document: vfs_removename

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562343-vfs_removename
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562343-vfs_removename

# vfs_removename

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Deprecated

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vfs_removename(const char *name);
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

vnode_update_identity() and vnode_create() make vfs_addname() unnecessary for kexts.
# Document: vn_revoke

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562348-vn_revoke
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562348-vn_revoke

# vn_revoke

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Invalidate all references to a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vn_revoke(vnode_t vp, int flags, vfs_context_t ctx);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to revoke.
- `flags`: Unused.
- `ctx`: Context against which to validate operation.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

0 always.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Reclaims the vnode, giving it deadfs vnops (though not halting operations which are already in progress). Also reclaims all aliased vnodes (important for devices). People holding usecounts on the vnode, e.g. processes with the file open, will find that all subsequent operations but closing the file fail.
# Document: vnode_issystem

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562350-vnode_issystem
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562350-vnode_issystem

# vnode_issystem

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Determine if a vnode is marked as a System vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_issystem(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to test.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Nonzero if the vnode is a system vnode, 0 if it is not.

# Document: vnode_clearfsnode

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562353-vnode_clearfsnode
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562353-vnode_clearfsnode

# vnode_clearfsnode

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Sets a vnode's filesystem-specific data to be NULL.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void vnode_clearfsnode(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose data to clear out.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

This routine should only be called when a vnode is no longer in use, i.e. during a VNOP_RECLAIM.

# Document: vnode_mount

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562358-vnode_mount
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562358-vnode_mount

# vnode_mount

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Get the mount structure for the filesystem that a vnode belongs to.

## Declaration

```objectivec
mount_t vnode_mount(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose mount to grab.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The mount, directly.

# Document: vfs_context_create

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562360-vfs_context_create
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562360-vfs_context_create

# vfs_context_create

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Create a new vfs_context_t with appropriate references held.

## Declaration

```objectivec
vfs_context_t vfs_context_create(vfs_context_t ctx);
```

## Parameters

- `ctx`: Context to copy, or NULL to use information from running thread.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

The new context, or NULL in the event of failure.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The context must be released with vfs_context_rele() when no longer in use.
# Document: vnode_update_identity

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562361-vnode_update_identity
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562361-vnode_update_identity

# vnode_update_identity

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Update vnode data associated with the vfs cache.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void vnode_update_identity(vnode_t vp, vnode_t dvp, const char *name, int name_len, uint32_t name_hashval, int flags);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode whose information to update.
- `dvp`: Parent to set on the vnode if VNODE_UPDATE_PARENT is used.
- `name`: Name to set in the cache for the vnode if VNODE_UPDATE_NAME is used. The buffer passed in can be subsequently freed, as the cache does its own name storage. String should be NULL-terminated unless length and hash value are specified.
- `name_len`: Length of name, if known. Passing 0 causes the cache to determine the length itself.
- `name_hashval`: Hash value of name, if known. Passing 0 causes the cache to hash the name itself.
- `flags`: VNODE_UPDATE_PARENT: set parent. VNODE_UPDATE_NAME: set name. VNODE_UPDATE_CACHE: flush cache entries for hard links associated with this file. VNODE_UPDATE_PURGE: flush cache entries for hard links and children of this file.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The vfs namecache is central to tracking vnode-identifying data and to locating files on the system. vnode_update_identity() is used to update vnode data associated with the cache. It can set a vnode's parent and/or name (also potentially set by vnode_create()) or flush cache data.

# Document: vfs_context_rele

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562367-vfs_context_rele
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562367-vfs_context_rele

# vfs_context_rele

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Release references on components of a context and deallocate it.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vfs_context_rele(vfs_context_t ctx);
```

## Parameters

- `ctx`: Context to release.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Always 0.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

A context should not be referenced after vfs_context_rele has been called.

Set flags indicating that a block device vnode has been mounted as a filesystem.

## Declaration

```objectivec
void vnode_setmountedon(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to set flags on, a block device.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

void.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

A block device marked as being mounted on cannot be opened.

# Document: vnode_hascleanblks

Source path: documentation/kernel/1562371-vnode_hascleanblks
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/1562371-vnode_hascleanblks

# vnode_hascleanblks

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Check if a vnode has clean buffers associated with it.

## Declaration

```objectivec
int vnode_hascleanblks(vnode_t vp);
```

## Parameters

- `vp`: The vnode to test.

<a id="return_value"></a>

## Return Value

Nonzero if there are clean blocks, 0 otherwise.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Note that this routine is unsynchronized; it is only a snapshot and its result may cease to be true at the moment it is returned..
